title: Elder Devasabha (II): Accomplished in right striving, practicing on the foundations of mindfulness, Filled with the flower of liberation, he will attain cessation, taintless.
content:
Elder Devasabha (II):

Accomplished in right striving, practicing on the foundations of mindfulness,
Filled with the flower of liberation, he will attain cessation, taintless.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these six impossible cases. What six? A person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the Teacher; a…
content: Bhikkhus, there are these six impossible cases. What six? A person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the Teacher; a person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the good Dhamma; a person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the Saṅgha; a person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the training; a person possessed of right view cannot revert to what should not be reverted to; a person possessed of right view cannot bring about an eighth state of existence. Bhikkhus, these are the six impossible cases.

title: One who is restrained in body, speech, and mind, Who does no evil deeds, Whose three doors are guarded, Him I call a brahmin. One…
content:
One who is restrained in body, speech, and mind,
Who does no evil deeds,
Whose three doors are guarded,
Him I call a brahmin.

One from whom one can learn the good Dhamma
Taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One,
One should venerate that person,
As a brahmin venerates the sacrificial fire.

One is not a brahmin because of matted hair,
Nor because of family or birth.
One in whom there is truth and Dhamma,
Who is pure — that one is a brahmin.

title: - Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Bhikkhus,…
content: - Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Bhikkhus, one who delights in the water element ... one who delights in the fire element ... one who delights in the air element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering.

title: A framework of sinews and bone, plastered with flesh and skin, The body is covered by a skin — it is not seen as it…
content:
A framework of sinews and bone, plastered with flesh and skin,
The body is covered by a skin — it is not seen as it really is.

Filled with a full belly: the liver, bladder, heart, lungs,
Kidneys and spleen, mucus, saliva, sweat, fat, blood, synovial fluid,
Bile, and serum.

From these nine streams, defilement constantly flows:
From the eyes, eye discharge; from the ears, ear discharge;
From the nose, nasal mucus; from the mouth, sometimes vomit,
Bile and phlegm; from the body, sweat and dirt.

title: ( Sakka ): Everyone should strive Until the goal is achieved. When the goal is achieved, One shines brilliantly. There is nothing better Than patience.
content:
( Sakka ):
Everyone should strive
Until the goal is achieved.
When the goal is achieved,
One shines brilliantly.
There is nothing better
Than patience.

title: Prince, having heard Brahmā's request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, Prince, I saw beings with…
content:
Prince, having heard Brahmā's request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, Prince, I saw beings with little dust in their eyes, with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties, with dull faculties, with good qualities, with bad qualities, easy to teach, hard to teach, and some who saw the danger in future rebirth and in faulty actions. Just as in a pond of blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses, some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, do not rise above the water, thrive while submerged; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, live reaching the water's surface; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, rise above the water and stand without being wetted by the water. So too, Prince, with the Buddha-eye I saw beings with little dust in their eyes... And, Prince, I spoke this verse to Brahmā Sahampati:

The door to the Deathless is open,
For those who are willing to hear.
Renounce your inaccurate faith.
Thinking of the trouble,
I did not want to teach
The supreme sublime Dhamma
Among humans.
(O Brahmā)

title: And, Mahānāma, how is a noble disciple possessed of virtue? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is virtuous, he lives restrained by the restraint of the…
content: And, Mahānāma, how is a noble disciple possessed of virtue? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is virtuous, he lives restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training in the training rules. Mahānāma, thus is a noble disciple possessed of virtue.

title: Four Right Efforts: Here, friends, a bhikkhu generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the non-arising of unarisen evil,…
content: Four Right Efforts: Here, friends, a bhikkhu generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the arising of unarisen wholesome states. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, expansion, cultivation, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states.

title: Elder Mahānāga: Those who have no respect for fellow celibates — They decline in the true Dhamma, like fish in shallow water. Those who have…
content:
Elder Mahānāga:

Those who have no respect for fellow celibates —
They decline in the true Dhamma, like fish in shallow water.

Those who have no respect for fellow celibates —
They do not grow in the true Dhamma, like rotten seed in a field.

Those who have no respect for fellow celibates —
They are far from Nibbāna, in the teaching of the Dhamma King.

Those who have respect for fellow celibates —
They do not decline in the true Dhamma, like fish in abundant water.

Those who have respect for fellow celibates —
They grow in the true Dhamma, like good seed in a field.

Those who have respect for fellow celibates —
They are close to Nibbāna, in the teaching of the Dhamma King.
